headline.text: The Spanish label says aspirin adds to celecoxib's gastrointestinal adverse-event risk, even at low aspirin doses.

reported.text: The Spanish label describes increased gastrointestinal ulceration or other gastrointestinal complications with coadministration.
The FDA label separately reports no interference with aspirin's cardioprotective antiplatelet effect in two studies at the stated doses.

claims.text: The Spanish label says aspirin, even at low doses, adds to gastrointestinal adverse-event risk with celecoxib.
claims.quote: La administración conjunta de celecoxib con ácido acetilsalicílico (incluso en pequeñas dosis) incrementa adicionalmente el riesgo de efectos adversos digestivos (ulceración gastrointestinal u otras complicaciones gastrointestinales).
claims.quoteEnglish: Coadministration of celecoxib with acetylsalicylic acid (even at low doses) further increases the risk of gastrointestinal adverse effects (gastrointestinal ulceration or other gastrointestinal complications).
claims.judgeRationale: The Spanish SmPC says coadministration with aspirin, even at low doses, further increases GI adverse-effect risk; the translation is faithful.

claims.text: The FDA label reports no interference with aspirin's antiplatelet effect in two studies using celecoxib 200–400 mg daily and aspirin 100–325 mg.
claims.quote: In two studies in healthy volunteers, and in patients with osteoarthritis and established heart disease respectively, celecoxib (200 mg to 400 mg daily) has demonstrated a lack of interference with the cardioprotective antiplatelet effect of aspirin (100 mg to 325 mg).
claims.judgeRationale: The FDA label reports two studies in which celecoxib 200-400 mg daily did not interfere with aspirin's (100-325 mg) cardioprotective antiplatelet effect.

pharmacistQuestions.text: The label describes this interaction, but there seem to be no human studies of it. How is it usually handled for someone like me?
Do any of my other medicines contain Aspirin or Celecoxib, or work the same way?
Does my dose, or the time between taking Aspirin and Celecoxib, change how much this matters?
